content:
The definition of the word ‘grandiose’ never ceases to be fascinating to me.

Compare this with the similar-looking, but ‘plainer and more innocent’ word, ‘grand.’

Notice how ‘grandiose’ itself is a word that got into English as a loanword from French, yet its actual meaning in English nowadays has such a negative connotation and so different from its French original. It’s also one of the most misused words (accidentally or not), especially among those who actually intend to mean ‘grand’ instead.

It’s almost as if the word itself is already a cheeky dig towards pretentious people who like to throw random, fancy-sounding foreign words in between their speeches just to present themselves as ‘more superior than others.’1

  1. Taiwanese would be familiar with the so-called Jingjing-speak (晶晶體). ↩︎
